previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of alcohol dependence, was admitted for alcohol withdrawal, chest pain, and an untreated pulmonary embolism from a prior admission where he left against medical advice. He presented with confusion, dizziness, right ankle pain from a recent fall, and neuropathic chest and shoulder pain. During his stay, he was treated for alcohol withdrawal with benzodiazepines, restarted on heart failure and anticoagulation therapy, and diagnosed with B12 deficiency and BPPV. He initially refused treatment and showed signs of depression and impaired decision-making, prompting a psychiatric evaluation and temporary legal intervention. Over time, he regained capacity, agreed to treatment, and was discharged to a shelter with a comprehensive medication plan including daily enoxaparin, oral B12, and plans for outpatient follow-up for mental health and substance use.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Other sprains and strains of ankle
Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ

___ homeless man with alcohol abuse, PE noncompliant

# Alcohol withdrawal: Pt with significant alcohol abuse history, 
drinks ___ pints daily. Last drink at noon on ___. Has had 
withdrawal seizures previously. Had very mild withdrawal 
symptoms, including tachycardia to the ___, diastolic HTN, and 
tremulousness. He was monitored on CIWA protocol and had minimal 
benzodiazepine requirements. His withdrawal symptoms resolved 
completely by the following morning and had no seizure activity. 
Therefore, he was discharged home. Metoprolol and thiamine, MVI, 
folic acid were continued.
. 
# Resolving pneumonia: Although CT abdomen showed RLL 
consolidation concerning for pneumonia, CXR looked improved from 
prior and his cough was also improving. He received 750mg iv 
levofloxacin in ED. Of note, quantiferon gold checked on 
previous admission in ___ was negative.  Given that the 
pneumonia was radiologically resolving and was clinically 
improved, antibiotics were not continued.
.  
# Chest pain: Has had chronic chest pain since ___ states 
that pain is the same. This admission, he ruled out for MI with 
two sets negative troponins. EKG is unchanged from prior without 
ischemic changes. During previous admission, CT C-spine showed 
DJD in C4-C7 and particularly narrowing of the left C4-C5 
foramina. As pt's pain distribution closely approximated the 
cutaneous distribution of recurrent nerves of the brachial 
plexus, his pain was felt to be ___ these neck findings. 
Pacemaker site appears clean/dry/intact without evidence of 
infection.  We continued lidoderm patch and gabapentin, and the 
pt had no further CP after leaving the ER.
.  
# Abdominal pain: Pt with mid-epigastric and left sided 
abdominal pain, which had improved by the time of admission. 
This was likely ___ alcoholic gastritis. CT abdomen showed no 
acute process. LFTs were unremarkable. Hct was 31 on discharge 
from last admission, now stable in high 20's. PPI was continued.
.  
# h/o pulmonary embolism: Pt has recently diagnosed PE ___ 
but per report was noncompliant with anticoagulation in the 
past. Given contraindications to coumadin therapy (pt has 
alcohol abuse with multiple falls), it was previously decided to 
discharge him on lovenox injections. Pt reports that he has been 
compliant with his lovenox recently, though he does have 
longstanding history of medication noncompliance. Lovenox was 
continued.
.  
# Atrial fibrillation: Pt with afib, previously on dabigatran, 
with which he was noncompliant. Now on Lovenox SQ for both PE 
and A fib. He is rate controlled on metoprolol.
.  
# Cardiomyopathy: Pt with EF 25%, s/p pacemaker placement.  We 
cont aspirin, ___, lasix.

# RLE pain: Pt has chronic right ankle pain radiating to knee. 
X-rays on previous admission were unremarkable. Brace had been 
provided but pt was noncompliant. Felt to have neuropathic pain. 
 We continued gabapentin.

# Depression: Pt with depression, history of noncompliance with 
meds and medical care. He was informed to f/u as outpatient with 
PCP for initiation of psych meds which he has not yet done.
